copies.headline: Adam's Kicker Didn't Show, Isaac Did
copies.body:
Will Reichard put up a zero, and that's the ballgame. Adam lost by 3.9 to a team averaging 104.8 a week, and the kicker spot alone was a 10.3-point swing to Isaac. Add T.J. Hockenson's 15.8 against Sam LaPorta's 6.5 and you've covered the margin twice over before anyone mentions Ja'Marr Chase going for 31.1. Adam won the backfield handily — Bucky Irving 21.0, Rico Dowdle 11.6 — but Jayden Daniels came in at 15.0 on a 22.8 projection and Kenneth Walker III managed 12.4 on 19.9, and the league's best offense turned in its second-worst week at 108.9.
Isaac won this one sideways. Javonte Williams produced 6.7 on a 20.1 projection, Jakobi Meyers gave him 4.4 while Dalton Kincaid scored 18.6 on the bench, and the Colts D/ST contributed a single point. He won anyway.
So Isaac is 4-4 on a two-game streak with a 31-57 all-play, still living on borrowed luck, and now leads the reigning champ 5-3 all-time. Our 21-point pick for Adam has aged badly.

copies.headline: Burrow Buries Grant, Flowers Never Showed
copies.body:
The quarterback slot decided this one before anything else got a vote. Joe Burrow put up 39.5, Kyler Murray managed 19.9, and that 19.6-point gap was already more than half the final margin. Logan then won the backfield by nine behind Braelon Allen and Jaylen Warren, took the receivers by nearly as much, and even cleared Grant by seven at kicker. Grant's only real wins came from the Commanders defense and Dallas Goedert, which is not a path to 146 points.
The killer was Zay Flowers: 20.1 projected, 0.0 actual. Twenty points of nothing, with Caleb Douglas and his 8.3 sitting there, and Patrick Mahomes stranded on the bench for 25.4 more. Logan had his own sin — Tyler Allgeier scored 36.1 in street clothes while Luther Burden III started — but when you're winning six of seven positions you get to leave points lying around.
Logan's at 3-5 with a 54-34 all-play, which means the record is a lie and everyone knows it. Grant drops to 4-4 and stays exactly what he's always been. We picked Grant by seven; we'd like that back.

copies.headline: Penix Goes Negative, CJ Goes Nowhere
copies.body:
CJ lost this at quarterback before anyone else touched the ball. Michael Penix Jr. finished at minus-1.9 on a 15.5 projection, a 17-point hole dug by a single roster spot, and in a game decided by 28.4 that's the whole argument. Christian got 19.4 from Trevor Lawrence and never had to do anything clever after that. Add Bhayshul Tuten's 29.9 — the best number on either roster — and the running back room was a 46.0-to-31.6 beating too.
CJ actually won three spots. The Steelers D/ST put up 16.0 against Seattle's 1.0 and Jason Sanders outkicked Brandon Aubrey, which is a nice trivia answer and nothing else. Parker Washington at 3.6 on a 16.0 projection and Jonathan Taylor at 6.7 did the rest of the damage. Three straight weeks under 100 for CJ now.
Christian's at 3-5 with the third-best scoring average in the league and an all-play of 54-34, which is the statistical definition of getting mugged weekly. We had him by 12; he took 28.4 instead.

copies.headline: Josh Allen Alone Survives Week 8's Blackout
copies.body:
Leif won this with one position and a prayer. Josh Allen's 26.6 was more than Kaleb got from his quarterback, both running backs and both receivers combined, and that QB gap — plus 17.6 — is the entire 1.9-point margin and then some. Everything else was a crime scene. Chris Godwin and Omar Cooper Jr. both put up zeroes on 10.6 projections, Kyle Pitts managed 2.6, and Jason Myers kicked in 1.7. Leif scored 64.7, his season low by 28, and still improved to 6-2.
Kaleb nearly stole it anyway because Harold Fannin went for 23.4 at tight end, a 20.8-point edge. What killed him was Tre Tucker's zero with Keenan Allen (13.7), Ladd McConkey (12.6) and Jordan Addison (11.6) all rotting on the bench. Any one of them wins the game. Drake London missing his projection by 16.1 didn't help.
We picked Kaleb by 7, which looks less wrong when you see he scored 62.7. Leif is 6-2 with an all-play of 43-45 and 2.1 wins of luck — the lovable basement dweller is getting away with something, and Kaleb, three straight 8-6 seasons deep, is the one paying for it.

copies.headline: Noah's Kicker And Defense Buried Mitchell
copies.body:
The skill positions were a coin flip. Noah won QB by 2.7, running back by 3.3, receiver by 3.6 — nothing you'd notice at the time. The game was decided by the two slots nobody drafts for: the Jaguars defense put up 21.0 against the Bengals' 2.0, and Chad Ryland outscored Tyler Loop 10.9 to 2.6. That's 27 points from kicker and defense alone, more than the 34.6 final margin needed. Noah actually lost the flex by eight with Hunter Henry's 6.0 and it didn't matter.
Mitchell got 24.8 from Jahmyr Gibbs and 20.9 from Matthew Golden and still lost by five touchdowns' worth. Jordan Mason's 2.0 on a 9.5 projection gutted the RB2 spot, and Travis Kelce sat on the bench with 11.7 while Tyler Warren managed 5.8. We picked Noah by nine; the mechanism was wrong, the direction wasn't.
Mitchell is 1-7 with a 30-58 all-play, dead last in the league and in the power rankings — the human coin flip has forgotten how to land. Noah, at 2-6 with 143.1, is doing the thing where he looks dead until January.

copies.headline: Peter Starts A Zero, John Starts Running
copies.body:
A zero at quarterback is not a bad week, it's a forfeit. Lamar Jackson posted 0.0 on a 22.2 projection, and Peter still had Justin Herbert on the bench doing nothing with his 7.8. That's 22 points of hole before anyone touched a football, and John only needed 8.3 from Matthew Stafford — his own worst starter — to clear the bar. Add Brock Bowers putting up 28.2 at flex against George Pickens' 6.8, and the 47-point margin was built on two lineup slots.
Peter actually won wide receiver by 10.5 on Tee Higgins' 37.5 and still lost by seven touchdowns' worth. Bijan Robinson's 7.6 on a 20.1 projection didn't help, nor did leaving Adonai Mitchell's 27.2 rotting behind Pickens. John's 165.1 is his third straight week trending up, and his all-play 61-27 says the 5-3 undersells him badly.
Peter's 45% all-play and +1.4 luck were always a bill coming due; it arrived at his brother's house. John leads it 7-3 now, and still won't shut up about it.

intro: Isaac survived Adam by 3.9, but the actual photo finish was Leif over Kaleb 64.66 to 62.74, a game that produced fewer combined points than John put up by himself in a 47-point demolition of Peter. Logan and Noah also cleared 143, which means half this slate was decided by double digits and the other half barely registered a pulse. Leif won and should probably never speak of it again.
